title: Shorthand syntax and what it expands to
objectives: Expand `?.`, `?.[]` and `?.()` into explicit checks, and predict where a chain short-circuits and where it still throws
Choose `??` or `||` (and `??=`, `||=`, `&&=`) by asking whether `0`, `""` or `false` is a real value
Predict destructuring results: defaults apply only to `undefined`, renames, rest, nested patterns, and `null` throwing
Write object literals with computed keys and spread, and predict which value wins when spread keys overlap — including a key present as `undefined`

options.text: `undefined` if `user` or `user.profile` is `null`/`undefined`; otherwise `user.profile.avatarUrl`
Exactly what `user && user.profile && user.profile.avatarUrl` gives
`user.profile.avatarUrl`, or `undefined` if any part of the access throws
`null` if any step is missing, otherwise `user.profile.avatarUrl`

questions.explanation: Each `?.` checks the value to its left for `null`/`undefined` and, if so, ends the whole expression as `undefined`. The `&&` chain differs: it stops at *any* falsy value and returns that value — `null`, `""`, `0` — not `undefined`. `?.` catches nothing: a getter that throws still throws. And it never produces `null`.

questions.prompt: A component calls `props.onChange?.(value)`. What does the `?.` guard against?

options.text: `onChange` being `null` or `undefined` — then the call is skipped and the expression is `undefined`
`onChange` not being a function, whatever its value
Both `props` and `onChange` being missing
Errors thrown inside `onChange`

questions.explanation: `fn?.()` checks only for `null`/`undefined`. If `onChange` is a string, the call still throws "is not a function" (MDN). It guards only the value immediately to its left, so a missing `props` needs `props?.onChange?.(value)`. And it has nothing to do with errors thrown by the callback itself.

questions.prompt: In `setForm({ ...form, [e.target.name]: e.target.value })`, what do the square brackets do?

options.text: Use the *value* of `e.target.name` (say `"email"`) as the key
Nothing — `{ e.target.name: value }` means the same thing
Wrap the value in a one-element array
Make the key optional, like `?:` in a type

questions.explanation: A computed key evaluates the expression in brackets and uses the result as the property name, so one handler updates whichever field fired. Without brackets, `{ e.target.name: value }` isn't a valid key — it's a `SyntaxError`. Because the spread comes first, the new key overrides the old value of that field.

questions.prompt: `const volume = saved.volume || 0.8;` — users who muted the player (`volume: 0`) find it un-muted after a reload. Which line fixes it?

options.text: `const volume = saved.volume ?? 0.8;`
`const volume = +saved.volume || 0.8;`
`const volume = saved.volume && 0.8;`
`const volume = saved.volume || 0.8 || 0;`

questions.explanation: `||` falls back on every falsy value, and `0` is falsy, so a muted player gets 0.8. `??` falls back only on `null`/`undefined`. Converting to a number first changes nothing (0 is still falsy); `&&` inverts the logic (it returns 0.8 for every non-zero saved volume, and `undefined` when nothing was saved); and an extra `|| 0` can never run, because `0.8` is truthy.

options.text: Only when `settings.theme` is `null` or `undefined`; otherwise neither the call nor the assignment happens
Always — the result is just discarded when `theme` is already set
Whenever `settings.theme` is falsy, including `""`
Only when needed, but `settings.theme` is always reassigned (to itself, when set)

questions.explanation: Logical assignment short-circuits: `x ??= y` behaves like `x ?? (x = y)`. When `x` is already non-nullish, the right side isn't evaluated and no assignment happens — MDN notes this is why `||=` on a truthy getter/setter property never calls the setter. Falling back on any falsy value is `||=`.

questions.prompt: Given `function paginate({ page = 1 } = {}) { return page; }`, which call throws?

options.text: `paginate(null)`
`paginate()`
`paginate(undefined)`
`paginate({})`

questions.explanation: Parameter defaults, like destructuring defaults, replace only `undefined`. `paginate()` and `paginate(undefined)` get `{}` and then `page = 1`; `paginate({})` gets `page = 1` directly. `paginate(null)` keeps `null` as the argument, and destructuring `null` is a `TypeError`. If `null` can arrive (JSON, a database row), normalise it first: `paginate(options ?? {})`.

questions.prompt: After adding `const label = user.nickname || user.name ?? "Anonymous";` the whole module fails to load. Why?

options.text: `??` can't be combined with `||` or `&&` without parentheses — it's a `SyntaxError`
It throws a `TypeError` at runtime when `user.nickname` is `null`
It loads fine; `??` simply binds tighter than `||`
`??` throws when its left side is `undefined`

questions.explanation: The language refuses to pick a precedence between `??` and `||`/`&&`, so `a || b ?? c` is a parse error and nothing in the file runs. Say which you meant: `(user.nickname || user.name) ?? "Anonymous"`. (Usually what you meant is `user.nickname ?? user.name ?? "Anonymous"` — chaining `??` with itself is allowed.)

questions.prompt: A reviewer suggests replacing `props.onSelect?.(item)` with `props.onSelect!(item)` "to make it stricter". What changes when `onSelect` isn't passed?

options.text: It now throws: `!` is erased at compile time, so the emitted code is a plain call
Nothing — `!` and `?.` both skip the call when the value is missing
It throws a clearer "onSelect is required" error from TypeScript at runtime
It fails to compile, because `onSelect` is optional

questions.explanation: TypeScript's non-null assertion `!` only tells the compiler "this isn't null" and disappears from the output — the code becomes `props.onSelect(item)` and throws `TypeError: props.onSelect is not a function`. TypeScript adds no runtime checks of its own, and it accepts the `!` on an optional prop: that's exactly what `!` is for. `?.` is the one that checks at runtime.

prompts.prompt: Call the optional `onSelect` callback only if the parent passed one.
prompts.explanation: `fn?.(args)` skips the call (and evaluates to `undefined`) when `fn` is `null`/`undefined`. It doesn't check that `fn` is a function, and it doesn't guard `props`.

prompts.prompt: Default the volume to 0.8, but keep a saved volume of `0` (muted).
prompts.explanation: `??` falls back only on `null`/`undefined`. `||` would treat `0` as missing and un-mute the player.

prompts.prompt: Read `id` as `userId`, default `role` to `"viewer"`, and collect every other field in `profile`.
prompts.explanation: In a pattern, `key: name` renames (it isn't a type annotation), `= value` is a default that applies only when the property is `undefined`, and `...name` gathers the remaining own enumerable properties into a new object. The rest element must come last.

prompts.prompt: One change handler for every input in the form: copy `form`, then set the field named by the input.
prompts.explanation: Square brackets make a computed key: the input's `name` attribute (`"email"`, `"phone"`) becomes the property name. The spread comes first so the new value wins over the copied one.

prompts.prompt: Compute the value for `key` only if the cache has nothing (`null`/`undefined`) stored for it.
prompts.explanation: `a ??= b` assigns only when `a` is nullish, and short-circuits: `compute(key)` doesn't run at all when a value is cached. `||=` would also recompute a cached `0` or `""`. (For a `Map` cache, use `has`/`get`/`set` — the collections unit covers why.)

snippets.question: What is logged?
snippets.explanation: No `?.` follows `items`, yet nothing throws: when `order?.` meets `null`, it short-circuits the *whole* chain to its right — `.items`, `[i++]` and `.sku` never run, so `i` is never incremented. Wrapping part of the chain in parentheses would end that protection: `(order?.items)[i++]` throws.

code: const s = { volume: 0, nickname: "", muted: false };
snippets.question: What are the two lines logged?
snippets.explanation: `||` replaces every falsy value, so the muted volume becomes 50 and `muted: false` becomes `true` — the opposite of what the user saved. `??` replaces only `null`/`undefined`, so it keeps `0` and `false`. (`s.nickname || "anon"` would likewise discard a deliberately empty nickname.)

snippets.question: What is logged?
snippets.explanation: A destructuring default applies only when the value is `undefined` — missing (`sort`) or explicitly `undefined`. `pageSize` is present with the value `null`, which counts as a value, so the default is skipped. APIs and databases send `null` all the time; use `res.pageSize ?? 20` when `null` should also fall back.

code: const saved = { fontSize: 16, theme: undefined }; // a cleared form field
snippets.question: What is logged?
acceptable: theme is undefined and fontSize is 16
snippets.explanation: Spread copies every own enumerable property, including one whose value is `undefined`, so the later `theme: undefined` overwrites `"light"`. The key keeps its first position. TypeScript doesn't flag this unless `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on. Merge field by field (`saved.theme ?? defaults.theme`) or drop `undefined` keys before spreading.
